 Petrol, Diesel Prices Today, November 18, 2026: Check Latest Rates in Delhi, Mumbai, Noida, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata and Other Cities

 Mumbai , November 18: Fuel rates remained largely unchanged across major Indian cities, although select locations reported revisions. Petrol is priced at Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi and Rs 111.21 in Mumbai, while diesel costs Rs 95.20 and Rs 97.83 per litre, respectively.    
 Oil prices edged lower on Wednesday as a sharp increase in US crude and fuel inventories reinforced concerns over supply, although escalating hostilities between the US and Iran and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited the decline. Brent crude futures fell 0.5% to $92.6 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude dropped 1.15% to $85.   
 US crude inventories increased by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended November 13, according to figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API), citing market sources. Gasoline stocks also climbed by 5.12 million barrels, while distillate inventories rose by 351,000 barrels, adding to signs of ample fuel availability in the world’s largest oil consumer.   
 However, geopolitical risks in the Middle East continued to underpin prices. Bahrain’s defence force said it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on the country, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, following an exchange of strikes between Washington and Tehran a day earlier. Iranian drones had targeted a US military radar installation in Bahrain, prompting US retaliatory strikes on a missile launch site on Iran’s Qeshm Island.   
 Shipping disruptions have added to concerns over the security of energy supplies. An LPG tanker was struck by a projectile off the coast of Oman while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, forcing its crew to evacuate. Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group also claimed responsibility for drone attacks on two pumping stations along Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, an alternative route for transporting crude that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz.   
 The latest price movement reflects competing forces in the oil market, with rising inventories and expectations of a global supply surplus counterbalancing the threat of further disruptions to Middle Eastern exports. Talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar have continued even as military confrontations have intensified, leaving traders cautious about the outlook for supply flows.   
 Check the latest petrol and diesel prices in Delhi, Mumbai, Noida, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad and other major cities.   
 Petrol Prices   
 Petrol prices remained largely unchanged across major Indian cities on Wednesday, November 18, with New Delhi retailing the fuel at Rs 102.12 per litre. Mumbai continued to have a higher rate of Rs 111.21 per litre, while Kolkata and Chennai recorded prices of Rs 113.51 and Rs 107.76 per litre, respectively.   
 Among other major cities, petrol was priced at Rs 110.44 per litre in Bengaluru, Rs 116.15 in Hyderabad and Rs 113.37 in Patna. Thiruvananthapuram recorded one of the highest rates among the listed cities at Rs 115.49 per litre, followed by Jaipur at Rs 112.69.   
 Price revisions were limited to a handful of cities. Bhubaneswar saw the steepest increase, with petrol becoming costlier by Rs 1.52 to Rs 110.49 per litre. Prices also rose by 34 paise in Lucknow to Rs 102.23 per litre, while Gurgaon recorded a reduction of 20 paise to Rs 102.77 and Jaipur saw a 50-paise decline to Rs 112.69.   
 In Noida, petrol was priced at Rs 101.96 per litre, while Chandigarh recorded a rate of Rs 101.54. The largely stable pricing across the country’s major urban centres indicates that most consumers saw no change in their petrol bills, despite the adjustments reported in a few cities.   
 Diesel Prices   
 Diesel prices remained largely unchanged across major Indian cities on Wednesday, November 18, with the fuel retailing at Rs 95.20 per litre in New Delhi. Mumbai recorded a price of Rs 97.83 per litre, while Kolkata and Chennai sold diesel at Rs 99.82 and Rs 99.55 per litre, respectively.   
 Among other major cities, diesel was priced at Rs 98.39 per litre in Bengaluru, Rs 104.23 in Hyderabad and Rs 99.36 in Patna. Thiruvananthapuram recorded the highest price among the listed cities at Rs 104.40 per litre, marginally ahead of Hyderabad. Bhubaneswar also reported a relatively high rate of Rs 102.15 per litre.   
 Price revisions were limited to a few cities. Bhubaneswar saw the steepest increase, with diesel becoming costlier by Rs 1.47 to Rs 102.15 per litre. Lucknow recorded a rise of 35 paise to Rs 95.71, while prices declined by Rs 1.17 in Bengaluru to Rs 98.39 per litre. Jaipur and Gurgaon also reported reductions of 47 paise and 20 paise, respectively.   
 In Noida, diesel was priced at Rs 95.44 per litre, matching Gurgaon’s revised rate. Chandigarh continued to have the lowest diesel price among the listed cities at Rs 89.47 per litre. Overall, rates remained stable across most major urban centres, with only a handful of cities reporting changes.
